criteria.name: artwork_craft
criteria.why: Slides 1, 5 and 6 pass most of the showstopper test. Slide 3's camera is a box and cylinder in a grey-middle room; slide 9's open transcript reads as clipping into the nosing; slide 2's pines are bare poles and its left wall a flat slab; slide 7's justices are small over dead floor; slide 4 has a plate behind its counter; slide 1's transcript is a plain block and its doors read as lit boxes.

criteria.name: deck_coherence
criteria.why: One hero on all nine frames carrying the case's state, a stair bookend, one world and palette, bluebonnet for certification only, and a declared value cut at 7. Frame 6 sits brightest and frame 4's facade a little outside.

criteria.name: claim_integrity
criteria.why: Every numeral traces and the October 9th orders were read in full. Framing is looser than the sources: Rule 203.6(a) is presented as the governing frame while the employer's c16 position that the rules would not allow it is cut; 'orders through October 9th' is wider than c30's single document; the case history and bench quotes rest on one article; slide 8 makes the schedule's 'will present' a completed fact; c1 and c2 were not re-fetched.

criteria.name: story_and_stakes
criteria.why: The deciders and the case are named in order and the status is honest. The stake for a Texan stays general and nothing says who a ruling would reach.

criteria.name: sequence_and_momentum
criteria.why: The hook earns the swipe, the turn at 6 to 7 is real and the close lands. Frame 5 mostly restates dates and 2 and 3 both spend themselves on the deposition room.

criteria.name: voice
criteria.why: Clean and plain within the house rules, but wire copy, with 'Courthouse News reports' and 'Drawn to illustrate.' repeated and little regional texture.

criteria.name: variety
criteria.why: The first court deck in the window with a new instrument and hero, on the house formula.

one_sentence_fix: Print the employer's c16 position beside Rule 203.6(a) on slide 6 so the frame shows what the court is weighing, and narrow 'orders through October 9th' to 'the court's October 9th orders list'.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: Box-and-cylinder camera in a grey-middle room with a lit band behind the dek; the transcript small and far back.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Model the camcorder, drop the back wall to black under one window rake, and pull the transcript into that pool at one scale.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: The open transcript reads as clipping into the nosing; a lighter band along the top edge.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Seat it on the tread face in front of the nosing with a contact shadow, move closer, and let the band fall into black.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: Bare pole pines and a flat pale left wall; a dead left third.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Model pine crowns against the seam and darken the room's left wall.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: Tiny justices on a thin strip over 40 percent dead floor.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Move forward and lower so the bench fills a third of the frame height.

artwork_weakest_frames.problem: A plate behind the counter and a mid-tone facade.
artwork_weakest_frames.fix: Reframe so the tower clears the counter zone or let that corner fall into shadow.
